# The Erechtheion

## Identity and consulted witness

Acropolis Museum, “The Erechtheion,” official thematic page, accessed September 8, 2026. [Selected digital carrier](https://www.theacropolismuseum.gr/en/node/16472). Accessed and saved 8 September 2026. The raw response is retained at `working/sources-texts-references/primary-texts/attica/acropolis-museum-erechtheion.html` (SHA-256 `0538e93a2a7f5c4faa991d88464e48be09185d3cb78fffa267456ecaf22b3c5b`). A saved page can contain more material than the selected reading; no whole-work reading is claimed.

## Source-specific reading

The museum describes a building of the final twenty years of the fifth century BCE, with Athena’s eastern chamber and a lower western chamber accommodating other cults. It explains the unusual plan through several cults, uneven ground and the sacred signs of the contest. The account lets a later built place be compared with the rival claims preserved in literary tellings.

Only the first two descriptive paragraphs bear this admission. The page’s attribution to Mnesikles is reported metadata, not independently settled here; neither its further sculpture discussion nor current collection-location statements are used by Attica. The building is a historical continuation of sacred memory, not another event in the Cecropian narrative.
